deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is folio 6 of Riemann's draft 'Mechanik des Ohres' (on the mechanics of the ear), published posthumously by Henle in 1867 and reprinted in the Gesammelte Werke. On the previous page Riemann argues against the view that the tensor tympani constantly varies the transmission ratio of the middle ear. He supposes a sentry (Schildwache) hearing a sound at 10 ft and at 20,000 ft. He assumes the ratio between air motion at the eardrum and stapes motion is the same at both distances.

(1) Order-of-magnitude estimate, completing the sentence from the previous page. Suppose the stapes-footplate displacements at 10 ft from the sentry are about the smallest visible to the naked eye. Then at 20,000 ft they would be just visible under 2000-fold magnification.
- Implicit step (mine): the displacement amplitude of a spherical sound wave falls off as 1/r, ignoring absorption.
- The middle-ear transmission is linear with a fixed ratio, so the stapes amplitude also scales as 1/r.
- Hence A(20000)/A(10) = 10/20000 = 1/2000.
- A motion 2000 times smaller than the naked-eye threshold needs 2000x magnification to be seen.
- The purpose is to show how extraordinarily small the motions are that the ossicular chain transmits faithfully.

(2) Section II, qualitative mechanical requirements.
(a) For the tympanic apparatus to transmit such tiny motions faithfully, as experience shows it does, its solid parts must fit exactly against each other at their points of contact. A body cannot pass motion to another if it stands off from it by more than the amplitude of the motion. Any gap or play larger than the vibration amplitude (about 1/2000 of a visible displacement, from step 1) would break transmission.
(b) Only a small part of the mechanical energy (Kraft = work/energy) of the sound motion may be lost to other work, such as stretching joint capsules and membranes, instead of reaching the labyrinth.
(c) The next page explains how such loss is avoided: the free rim of the oval-window membrane (annular ligament) is extremely narrow.

No formulas are written on the page; the only quantitative content is the 1/r scaling and the factor 2000.
errors: No mathematical error. The 1/r amplitude law is implicit and neglects atmospheric absorption and ground effects. It is also not obvious that a sound is audible at 20,000 ft at all; Riemann takes that from the empirical example (presumably the sentry hearing distant signals) on earlier pages.
The premise that stapes motion at 10 ft is 'just visible with the naked eye' is a rough guess, not derived. Riemann marks it 'wahrscheinlich'.

results.what: Amplitude of stapes vibration scales inversely with distance from the source; the ratio of distances 20000:10 gives a 2000-fold reduction, used to estimate the minuteness of ossicular motion
results.modern_name: Spherical spreading (inverse-distance law for pressure/displacement amplitude) combined with linear middle-ear transfer
results.usually_credited_to: Classical acoustics (18th-19th c.); the application to ossicular amplitudes is part of Riemann's published 'Mechanik des Ohres' (1867)

results.what: Requirement that the ossicles fit together without play larger than the vibration amplitude, and that little energy be lost to capsules and membranes
results.modern_name: Contact conditions / efficiency of middle-ear impedance transformation (ossicular-chain mechanics)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1866/67), discussed alongside Helmholtz's 'Mechanik der Gehörknöchelchen' (1868)

deep.surprise_reason: This page is part of Riemann's posthumously published 'Mechanik des Ohres' (Henle 1867, Gesammelte Werke). Its content is an elementary scaling estimate and qualitative physiological-mechanical reasoning, already known as his.

checkable.asserts: The distance ratio 20,000 ft / 10 ft equals the required magnification factor 2000
Under the 1/r amplitude law, the amplitude ratio equals the inverse distance ratio
The amplitude at 20,000 ft is 1/2000 of the amplitude at 10 ft

transcription_corrections: 'kleiner Theil der wahrnehmbaren[?] Kraft' should read 'kleiner Theil der mechanischen Kraft der Schallbewegung'; the image shows 'mechanischen', not 'wahrnehmbaren'.
The marginal note '[Fuß' corresponds to the inserted word 'Fuß' after '20,000'; the insertion is correctly placed.
'wie er es der Erfahrung nach thut' is correct as transcribed.
